newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN chief points the way to sanctions on Angola's UNITA.
newsitem.headline: UN chief points the way to sanctions on Angola's UNITA.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Friday pointed the way towards international sanctions against Angola's UNITA movement, saying they had not complied with 1994 peace accords.

Annan, in a written report, said he was confident the Security Council would "continue to exercise its authority and take all necessary steps to ensure full compliance with its decisions." He said "last-minute half-hearted concessions by UNITA, under pressure and on the eve of Security Council deliberations are no longer acceptable."
The council had threatened sanctions against UNITA if it did not comply with its demands by the time Annan issued his report and diplomats said these would be discussed next week.

They probably would include a travel ban against UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi and other leaders. Other measures, such as freezing UNITA bank accounts abroad might not be enacted until a later date because they are difficult to enforce, the envoys said.

The council has demanded of UNITA that it demilitarize all its forces, transform of its radio station into a non-partisan broadcasting facility and cooperate fully in extending government administration throughout the country as required in 1994 peace agreements signed in Lusaka, Zambia.

After two decades of civil war UNITA, the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola, entered into a unity government in April with the ruling MPLA, the Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola. But UNITA still controls about 70 percent of the country, and only a minority of its fighters have been demobilized and incorporated into a national army.
